issues.description: Arbitrary-class instantiation RCE remains open: PropertyFactory.createProperty and the XML/YAML/properties parsers and web ConsoleOperations still do Class.forName(userType).newInstance()/getConstructor(...).newInstance(...) with no isAssignableFrom type check, so an attacker controlling the property/flipstrategy type can still load and instantiate arbitrary classes.

Fix is symptom-scoped to the single taint trace ending at PropertyClass.fromString; the official fix restricts loaded classes to Property/FlippingStrategy subtypes at every instantiation sink, which our patch does not replicate.

Switching to the thread context classloader (with fallback) changes class-resolution semantics versus the original single-arg Class.forName and could resolve differently in some container/classloader setups.

result.root_cause: Untrusted, externally-supplied class names are passed to Class.forName and then instantiated (newInstance / getConstructor().newInstance()) with no restriction that the resolved type belongs to an expected supertype, allowing attacker-controlled code execution.
result.summary: Our patch only hardens the single PropertyClass.fromString sink named in the taint trace, switching to a non-initializing Class.forName so the observed static-initializer payload no longer fires (POV stops, regressions pass). But it does not close the vulnerability class: the official fix adds isAssignableFrom type guards at every instantiation sink (PropertyFactory, XmlParser, YamlParser, PropertiesParser, MappingUtil, ConsoleOperations), all of which still call newInstance on attacker-controlled class names in our tree. It is a weaker subset of the reference fix and leaves real code-injection paths reachable.
